text: Users can log in with an identifier (username, email, or phone) plus password, or via social accounts like Facebook/X
quote: You built an awesome app and you want to add user authentication and authorization. Your users should be able to log in either with an identifier (username, email, or phone number) and password or with their social accounts

text: Lets you secure your own API using the OAuth 2.0 protocol
quote: You built an API and you want to secure it with OAuth 2.0.

text: Single sign-on lets users authenticate once and access all apps within the same tenant
quote: Auth0 Single Sign-On (SSO) lets users authenticate once and access all applications in the same tenant without re-entering credentials.

text: Supports many MFA factors: push, SMS, voice, OTP, WebAuthn (keys/biometrics), email, Cisco Duo, recovery codes
quote: Auth0 supports a variety of MFA factors, including: Push notifications, SMS notifications, Voice notifications, One-time passwords, WebAuthn with security keys, WebAuthn with device biometrics, Email notifications, Cisco Duo security, Recov

text: Organizations feature represents business customers/partners and manages their membership
quote:
Auth0 customers can use Organizations to:

*   Represent their business customers and partners in Auth0 and manage their membership.
*   Configure branded, federated login flows for each business.

text: Lets you configure branded, federated login flows for each business organization
quote: Configure branded, federated login flows for each business.

text: RBAC lets you group users into roles and assign permissions to those roles for authorization
quote: When using RBAC for Role Management, you analyze the needs of your users and group them into roles based on common responsibilities. You then assign one or more roles to each user and one or more permissions to each role.

text: Client-credentials/M2M flow for CLIs, daemons, and backend services to authenticate without a user
quote: This flow is best suited for Machine-to-Machine (M2M) applications, such as CLIs, daemons, or backend services

text: Device Authorization Flow lets input-constrained devices (smart TVs, media consoles) authorize via a linked device
quote: Learn how the Device Authorization flow works and why you should use it for input-constrained devices, such as smart TVs and media consoles.

text: Import mode lets you gradually migrate users from an external store to Auth0 as they log in
quote: Gradually migrate users from your external user store to Auth0 as they log in by enabling import mode on your custom database connection.

text: Bulk import and export of user data, including automatic migration between stores
quote: Migrate your user data into and out of Auth0 with automatic migration and bulk imports and exports.

text: Log streaming exports tenant auth/admin logs to an external log analysis or SIEM service
quote: Auth0's log streaming service allows you to export tenant logs to a log analysis service. You can choose the content type and form and preview the payload using the Auth0 Dashboard.

text: Auth0 MCP Server lets AI tools manage the tenant via natural language: create apps, deploy Actions, debug logs, manage users, using OAuth device auth
quote: The Auth0 Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server connects AI agents to your Auth0 tenant, allowing them to perform complex, multi-step operations in Auth0 such as creating applications, managing users, or deploying Actions.

text: Private Cloud managed deployment on AWS/Azure offers isolated environments with dev instances and Geo-HA add-ons
quote: A dedicated, managed cloud service running on AWS providing isolation, higher performance, dev instances, Geo-HA add-ons and more

text: Universal Login can be embedded in AI agents to verify user identity across social, enterprise, and custom identity providers
quote: Integrate Auth0's Universal Login into your AI agents to verify user identity, with support for social, enterprise, and custom identity providers.

text: AI agents can call first-party APIs on the user's behalf via OAuth 2.0 while preserving the user's context/scope
quote: Enable AI agents to securely call first-party APIs on the user’s behalf using OAuth 2.0. This ensures that the user’s context is maintained, preventing agents from having broad, unrestricted access to user data.

text: Token Vault obtains, stores, and refreshes tokens so agents can call third-party APIs (Google, Slack, GitHub) without handling raw credentials
quote: Auth0's Token Vault manages obtaining, storing, and refreshing API tokens, allowing your agents to interact with third-party APIs without handling sensitive credentials or API keys directly.

text: CIBA lets agents request out-of-band user approval (push/SMS/email) for sensitive actions even when the app isn't active
quote: Using standards like CIBA (Client-Initiated Backchannel Authentication), agents can request approval for sensitive operations via push notifications, SMS, or email

text: Auth0 FGA enforces fine-grained, document-level access control within RAG pipelines
quote: Enforce fine-grained, document-level access control within your Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines using Auth0 FGA.

text: Each AI agent can be given its own unique digital identity for scoped, secure access to APIs/apps/MCP servers
quote: Give each agent a unique digital identity for more secure access to APIs, apps, and MCP servers.

quote:

text: Supports SAML-based authentication for web apps
quote: You have a web app that needs to authenticate users using Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML)

text: Passwordless login via one-time codes delivered by email or SMS
quote: You believe passwords are broken and you want your users to log in with one-time codes delivered by email or SMS.

text: Detects breached credentials and can notify/block affected users from logging in
quote: If one of your user's email addresses is compromised in some site's public data breach, you want to be notified, and you want to notify the users and/or block them from logging in

text: Proactively blocks suspicious IP addresses after consecutive failed login attempts to prevent brute-force/DDoS
quote: You want to act proactively to block suspicious IP addresses if they make consecutive failed login attempts, in order to avoid DDoS attacks.

text: Federates an organization's enterprise directory so employees can log into internal and third-party apps with existing credentials
quote: You are part of a large organization that wants to federate your existing enterprise directory service to allow employees to log in to the various internal and third-party applications using their existing enterprise credentials.
